subject: humanities
notes: In ancient Mesopotamia, scribes pressed wedge-shaped marks into tablets of wet clay.
In ancient Egypt, scribes wrote with ink on sheets made from the papyrus plant, which grew along the Nile.
In China during the Shang dynasty, inscriptions were carved on turtle shells and the shoulder bones of oxen.
In parts of South and Southeast Asia, texts were written on dried palm leaves for many centuries.
stem: The student wants to make a generalization about the materials on which early writing was recorded. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Early writing was recorded on a wide range of materials, including clay tablets, sheets of papyrus, turtle shells and ox bones, and dried palm leaves.
choices.B: Scribes in ancient Mesopotamia pressed wedge-shaped marks into wet clay, while scribes in ancient Egypt wrote with ink on papyrus.
choices.C: During China's Shang dynasty, inscriptions were carved on turtle shells and on the shoulder bones of oxen.
choices.D: Texts were written on dried palm leaves for many centuries in parts of South and Southeast Asia.

explanation.why: A generalization is a broad statement that covers many cases. The notes describe four different regions, so the best choice draws a general conclusion that all of them support: early writing appeared on many kinds of materials.
explanation.A: Correct. It makes a broad claim about early writing and supports it with materials from all four notes.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It compares two specific cultures instead of drawing a general conclusion. It uses more than one note, which makes it tempting, but it stays at the level of particular cases.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It reports a single case from China and makes no general claim.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It reports a single case from South and Southeast Asia and makes no general claim.

checks.note: Best fit on the text alone.
